title: Kleingarten in Berlin - Quick Summary
items: **Berlin has 1,038 allotment colonies with about 70,000 plots**, covering roughly 2,900 hectares. The supply is wildly uneven: Pankow holds 10,258 plots and Treptow-Köpenick 9,011, while the whole of Friedrichshain-Kreuzberg has 228.

**You do not apply to the city, you register with your district association.** Each Bezirksverband der Gartenfreunde keeps its own waiting list and offers plots in registration order. Registration usually costs a small fee, for example 20 euros in Spandau and 50 euros in Lichtenberg.

**Expect years, not months.** The associations themselves quote at least 3 to 4 years in Lichtenberg and around 5 years in Spandau, and inner-city lists move slower than the S-Bahn belt. Registering now beats registering next spring, because the queue is ordered by date.

**Budget around 4,000 euros to take over a plot** for the previous tenant's Laube, trees and plantings, then roughly 700 euros a year for lease, fees, water and electricity. The lease itself is capped by federal law; the takeover valuation is the real cost.

**The rules are strict and enforced:** a plot should not exceed 400 square metres, the Laube stays under 24 square metres including its covered seating, at least one third of the garden must grow fruit and vegetables, and living in the Laube is not allowed.
